sonnet.reason: Both describe combative, forceful, compromise-rejecting behaviour, but militant is tied to zealous devotion to a cause and policing the lukewarm, while aggressive is a general confrontational style for getting what one wants.
Both involve refusing compromise, but militant adds aggressive, combative zeal against opponents and the lukewarm, while unyielding is just firm holding of a position without that aggression.
Both involve combative aggression toward others, but militant is cause-driven uncompromising zeal while confrontational is a general taste for conflict and arguments regardless of any cause.

Both describe fervent, crusading commitment to a cause and intolerance of lukewarmness, but militant stresses combative, uncompromising aggression against opponents while zealous stresses passionate fervor and heat.

Both involve fierce, uncompromising loyalty to a cause or side, but militant stresses aggressive combative zeal for any cause, while partisan stresses political side-taking, party-line conformity and bias, so each adds something the other lacks.

Both involve an uncompromising, hard stance, but militant is aggressive zeal for a cause against opponents, while unforgiving is holding grievances and refusing to pardon wrongdoers; neither implies the other.

Both involve strong advocacy, but militant is combative, uncompromising zeal for a cause against opponents, while opinionated is holding and voicing firm views on many topics without necessarily being aggressive or uncompromising.
Both involve refusing to compromise, but militant is aggressive zeal for a cause against opponents, while rigid is inflexible adherence to a method or plan; neither implies the other.
Both refuse compromise, but militant is about combative, aggressive zeal against opponents, while fundamentalist is about rigid adherence to basic principles without necessarily being aggressive.
